messages:
Maya: Quick update from the onboarding call with Aurora Bank. They want two must-haves before signing:
1) per-tenant "emergency legal hold" that overrides retention/TTL
2) rapid BYOK escrow with attestations (they expect a 7-day window for exports)
They asked about pricing / whether this is in Dedicated package or charged separately.

Sam: Important: they repeatedly said "no retention gaps" during the demo. Can we scope a minimal API that satisfies SOC2 evidence and exportability? We need an ROI calc vs storage delta.

Ellen: Legal note: if we expose a control-plane hold, it must be auditable (who/when/why) and we need RBAC so only delegated legal/admins can toggle. Also exports under hold may have jurisdictional implications.

Diego: Infra reality check: our lifecycle job currently deletes per prefix on a cron. To guarantee holds we need a fast path that marks objects immutable at object-store level or skips deletion for held prefixes. That changes lifecycle complexity and metrics.

ops-bot: FYI: existing cold-archive retention is enforced by S3 lifecycle; we can add object tags to opt-out but will need a rehydration policy and monitoring alarms.

Sam: Propose MVP split:
- Phase A (3 wks): control-plane flag + audit trail + search filter for held items + export pipeline tweak to include hold metadata
- Phase B (6-8 wks): BYOK escrow tooling + per-tenant rotation window + attestation docs
Phase A could be offered as "Enterprise standard"; Phase B as "Enterprise Plus" or add-on.

Maya: Customer is price-sensitive but will accelerate if Phase A + a 90-day escrow pilot included. They said they'd consider an anchor deal if we commit to Phase B timeline.

Ellen: From compliance: we need acceptance criteria for SOC2 mapping before we promise:
- holds survive restore/backfill
- holds appear in evidence exports as an immutable field
- RBAC audit logs for set/unset actions retained for X years
Add these to the spike definition.

Sam: Draft acceptance checklist (short):
- API to set/unset holds with reason, created_by, created_at, expires_at
- immutable audit_id returned and stored in evidence ledger
- search/index exposes held-flag and hold-reason for exports
- lifecycle engine ignores held prefixes for retention period
- integration test: create hold -> run lifecycle job -> confirm objects persist

Diego: Estimate: Phase A spike + 2 sprints to deliver = ~5 dev-weeks (including infra & e2e). Phase B = 10-12 dev-weeks plus security review.

Maya: Sales asks for a written commitment timeline. We should ask for a refundable deposit / LOI for anchoring to prioritize Phase B.

Sam: Decision: run a 5-day spike starting Monday to validate lifecycle skip and audit-trail plumbing. If spike proves low-risk, fast-track Phase A. Need product + compliance signoff by end of next week.

compliance-bot: Ticket created: C-9001 "spike: emergency-legal-hold + evidence-export-mapping" assigned to Diego. Due 2026-03-18.

Ellen: I'll draft SOC2 acceptance mapping and a list of tests. Add me to C-9001.

Maya: I'll push Aurora for an LOI and ask about a deposit to cover expedited escrow work.

Sam: Quick API sketch for discussion:
```
PUT /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/holds/{hold_id}
Body:
{ "active": true, "reason": "litigation-2026-03", "created_by": "legal@aurora.com", "expires_at": null }
Response: 200 { "hold_id": "h-20260310", "audit_id": "audit-0f9c" }
```
Make sure audit_id is replicated to export ledger.

ops-bot: Note: will need an ops-runbook change to restore holds after bucket restores; flagging runbook ticket R-7722.

Sam: OK - pairing session tomorrow 10am PT (Sam + Diego + Ellen) to finalize spike scope. If spike passes, we mark Phase A for next sprint and announce pricing options.

Maya: Thanks all. Will circle back after LOI update. :raised_hands:
